## After Excel Manual Labeling Load ID 1 (Resident - Rangeshift) - CWD Positive

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
citation("ggplot2")
packageVersion("ggplot2")
library(janitor)

# Load the data with tab separator
# Load CSV with default comma separator
deer_data_labels <- read.csv("<LOCAL_PATH>", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

colnames(deer_data_labels)

# Convert to POSIXct format
deer_data_labels$date_time <- as.POSIXct(deer_data_labels$datetime, format = "%m/%d/%y%H:%M", tz = "UTC")


# Check if the dataset is empty
if(nrow(deer_data_labels) == 0) {
  stop("Dataset is empty! Check file path and delimiter.")
}

# Print first few rows to inspect data
print(head(deer_data_labels))

# Automatically clean column names
deer_data_labels <- deer_data_labels %>% clean_names()

# Print cleaned column names
print(colnames(deer_data_labels))

# Check unique IDs
print(unique(deer_data_labels$id))

# Ensure "id" column is treated as character
deer_data_labels$id <- as.character(deer_data_labels$id)

# Re-check unique IDs
print(unique(deer_data_labels$id))

# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Function to create an interactive plot for a single deer
location_plot_interactive <- function(deer_data) {
  gg <- ggplot(data = deer_data, 
             aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, 
                 color = movement_behavior, text = paste("Date:", date))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  geom_path(alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = paste("Movement of Deer ID:", unique(deer_data$id)),
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", color = "Movement Behavior") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Resident" = "blue", 
                                "RangeShift" = "red", 
                                "Transition to RangeShift" = "orange",
                                "Transition to Resident" = "green"))

  # Convert ggplot to interactive plotly object
  ggplotly(gg, tooltip = "text")  # Enables hover info
}

# Create and display the interactive plot for the single ID in the dataset
location_plot_interactive(deer_data_labels)

# Function to create a static GGplot2 plot for a single deer
location_plot_static <- function(deer_data) {
  ggplot(data = deer_data, 
         aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = movement_behavior)) +
    geom_path(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +  # Connects movement paths
    geom_point(aes(size = 2), alpha = 0.8) +  # Plot individual points
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Movement of Deer ID:", unique(deer_data$id)),
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude",
         color = "movement_behavior") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Resident" = "blue", 
                                  "RangeShift" = "red", 
                                  "Transition to RangeShift" = "orange",
                                  "Transition to Resident" = "green"))
}

# Create and display the plot for the single ID in the dataset
location_plot_static(deer_data_labels)


```

```{r}
deer_data_labels <- read.csv("<LOCAL_PATH>", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


# Check if the dataset is empty
if(nrow(deer_data_labels) == 0) {
  stop("Dataset is empty! Check file path and delimiter.")
}

# Print first few rows to inspect data
print(head(deer_data_labels))

# Automatically clean column names
deer_data_labels <- deer_data_labels %>% clean_names()

# Print cleaned column names
print(colnames(deer_data_labels))

# Check unique IDs
print(unique(deer_data_labels$id))

# Ensure "id" column is treated as character
deer_data_labels$id <- as.character(deer_data_labels$id)

# Re-check unique IDs
print(unique(deer_data_labels$id))


# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Function to create an interactive plot for a single deer
location_plot_interactive <- function(deer_data) {
  gg <- ggplot(data = deer_data, 
               aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, 
                   color = migration_status, text = paste("Date:", date))) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +  # Plot individual points
    geom_path(alpha = 0.5) +  # Connect movement path
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Movement of Deer ID:", unique(deer_data$id)),
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude",
         color = "Migration Status") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Resident" = "blue", 
                                  "Migratory" = "red", 
                                  "Transition to Migratory" = "orange",
                                  "Transition to Resident" = "green"))
  
  # Convert ggplot to interactive plotly object
  ggplotly(gg, tooltip = "text")  # Enables hover info
}

# Create and display the interactive plot for the single ID in the dataset
location_plot_interactive(deer_data_labels)


# Function to create a static GGplot2 plot for a single deer
location_plot_static <- function(deer_data) {
  ggplot(data = deer_data, 
```
```{r}
         aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = migration_status)) +
    geom_path(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +  # Connects movement paths
    geom_point(aes(size = 2), alpha = 0.8) +  # Plot individual points
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Movement of Deer ID:", unique(deer_data$id)),
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude",
         color = "Migration Status") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Resident" = "blue", 
                                  "Migratory" = "red", 
                                  "Transition to Migratory" = "orange",
                                  "Transition to Resident" = "green"))
}

# Create and display the plot for the single ID in the dataset
location_plot_static(deer_data_labels)

```

```{r}
# Load CSV with default comma separator

  stop("Dataset is empty! Check file path and delimiter.")
}

print(head(deer_data_labels))

deer_data_labels <- deer_data_labels %>% clean_names()

print(colnames(deer_data_labels))

print(unique(deer_data_labels$id))


# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Function to create an interactive plot for a single deer
location_plot_interactive <- function(deer_data) {
  gg <- ggplot(data = deer_data, 
               aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, 
                   color = migration_status, text = paste("Date:", date))) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +  # Plot individual points
    geom_path(alpha = 0.5) +  # Connect movement path
    theme_minimal() +

                                  "Migratory" = "red", 
                                  "Transition to Migratory" = "orange",
                                  "Transition to Resident" = "green"))
  
  # Convert ggplot to interactive plotly object

}
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(janitor)

# Load the data with tab separator
# Load CSV with default comma separator
deer_data_labels <- read.csv("<LOCAL_PATH>", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```


```{r}
# Convert to POSIXct format
deer_data_labels$date_time <- as.POSIXct(deer_data_labels$datetime, format = "%m/%d/%y%H:%M", tz = "UTC")



# Check if the dataset is empty
if(nrow(deer_data_labels) == 0) {
  stop("Dataset is empty! Check file path and delimiter.")
}

# Print first few rows to inspect data
print(head(deer_data_labels))

# Automatically clean column names
deer_data_labels <- deer_data_labels %>% clean_names()

# Print cleaned column names
print(colnames(deer_data_labels))

# Check unique IDs
print(unique(deer_data_labels$id))

# Ensure "id" column is treated as character
deer_data_labels$id <- as.character(deer_data_labels$id)

# Re-check unique IDs
print(unique(deer_data_labels$id))

# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Function to create an interactive plot for a single deer
location_plot_interactive <- function(deer_data) {
  gg <- ggplot(data = deer_data, 
               aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, 
                   color = migration_status, text = paste("Date:", date))) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +  # Plot individual points
    geom_path(alpha = 0.5) +  # Connect movement path
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Movement of Deer ID:", unique(deer_data$id)),
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude",
         color = "Migration Status") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Resident" = "blue", 
                                  "Migratory" = "red", 
                                  "Transition to Migratory" = "orange",
                                  "Transition to Resident" = "green"))
  
  # Convert ggplot to interactive plotly object
  ggplotly(gg, tooltip = "text")  # Enables hover info
}

# Create and display the interactive plot for the single ID in the dataset
location_plot_interactive(deer_data_labels)

# Function to create a static GGplot2 plot for a single deer
location_plot_static <- function(deer_data) {
  ggplot(data = deer_data, 
         aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = movement_behavior)) +
    geom_path(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +  # Connects movement paths
    geom_point(aes(size = 2), alpha = 0.8) +  # Plot individual points
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Movement of Deer ID:", unique(deer_data$id)),
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude",
         color = "movement_behavior") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Resident" = "blue", 
                                  "Dispersal" = "red", 
                                  "Transition to Dispersal" = "orange",
                                  "Transition to Resident" = "green"))
}

# Create and display the plot for the single ID in the dataset
location_plot_static(deer_data_labels)
```

```{r}
    geom_path(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +  # Connects movement paths
    geom_point(aes(size = 2), alpha = 0.8) +  # Plot individual points
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Movement of Deer ID:", unique(deer_data$id)),
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude",
         color = "Migration Status") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Resident" = "blue", 
                                  "Migratory" = "red", 
                                  "Transition to Migratory" = "orange",
                                  "Transition to Resident" = "green"))
}

location_plot_static(deer_data_labels)
```

## Trying Levelle function for Segmentation
```{r}
library(adehabitatLT)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# #Assuming you already have an ltraj object (ltraj_obj) from your deer data:
# ltraj_obj <- as.ltraj(xy = deer_final_corrected_filtered2[, c("x", "y")],
#                       date = deer_final_corrected_filtered2$date,
#                       id = as.character(deer_final_corrected_filtered2$id))

# Remove rows with missing R2n values
df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(R2n))

# Confirm there are no NA values in the R2n column
if(any(is.na(df$R2n))) {
  cat("There are still NA values in R2n\n")
} else {
  cat("No NA values in R2n\n")
}

# Or simply use summary() to inspect the column:
summary(df$R2n)


# List of unique IDs
ids <- unique(df$id)

# Function to process each ID individually
process_id <- function(myid, Lmin = 10, K = 3, downsample_by = 10) {
  cat("Processing ID:", myid, "\n")
  # Subset data for this ID
  subset_data <- df %>% filter(id == myid)
  
  # Optional: Downsample if the series is very long (adjust 'downsample_by' as needed)
  if(nrow(subset_data) > 1000) {
    subset_data <- subset_data[seq(1, nrow(subset_data), by = downsample_by), ]
  }
  
  # Run lavielle on the R2n series for this ID
  seg <- try(lavielle(subset_data$R2n, Lmin = Lmin, K = K, plotit = FALSE))
  if (inherits(seg, "try-error")) {
    cat("Error in lavielle for ID:", myid, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Extract segmentation path for K segments
  fp <- findpath(seg, K)
  
  # Return a list with ID, segmentation result, and the processed subset data
  list(
    id = myid,
    segmentation = fp,
    data = subset_data
  )
}

# Process all IDs using purrr::map
results <- map(ids, process_id)

# Optionally remove any NULLs (if some IDs failed processing)
results <- compact(results)

# Example: Plot segmentation for a specific ID, say the first one in the list

  id1 <- results[[1]]
  plot(id1$segmentation)
  # You can also visualize the movement path colored by the segmentation if you have spatial coordinates:
  ggplot(id1$data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_path(aes(color = as.factor(burst)), size = 1) +
    geom_point() +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Movement Trajectory for ID", id1$id),
         color = "Segment")
}
```

## Classifying Migration
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(adehabitatLT)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)

# Assume that df is created from your ltraj object:
# df <- ld(ltraj_obj)
# Ensure no NA values in R2n:
df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(R2n))

# List of unique IDs
ids <- unique(df$id)

# Define a classification function for each segment.
# Note: Threshold values here are placeholders.
classify_segment <- function(segment_data) {
  segment_data <- segment_data[order(segment_data$date), ]
  duration <- as.numeric(difftime(max(segment_data$date), min(segment_data$date), units = "days"))
  total_disp <- max(segment_data$R2n) - min(segment_data$R2n)
  slope <- total_disp / duration
  
  # Placeholder thresholds:
  if(total_disp < 500) {
    return("Resident")
  } else if(slope < 50) {
    return("Nomadism")
  } else if(slope >= 50 & slope < 100) {
    return("Dispersal")
  } else if(slope >= 100 & duration < 30) {
    return("Migration")
  } else if(slope >= 100 & duration >= 30 & total_disp < 5000) {
    return("Partial Migration")
  } else if(slope >= 100 & duration >= 30 & total_disp >= 5000) {
    return("Facultative Migration")
  } else {
    return("Mixed Migration")
  }
}

# Function to process each ID individually.
process_id <- function(myid, Lmin = 10, K = 3, downsample_by = 10) {
  cat("Processing ID:", myid, "\n")
  # Subset data for this ID:
  subset_data <- df %>% filter(id == myid)
  
  # Optional: Downsample if the series is very long:
  if(nrow(subset_data) > 1000) {
    subset_data <- subset_data[seq(1, nrow(subset_data), by = downsample_by), ]
  }
  
  # Run lavielle on the R2n series for this ID:
  seg <- try(lavielle(subset_data$R2n, Lmin = Lmin, K = K, plotit = FALSE))
  if (inherits(seg, "try-error")) {
    cat("Error in lavielle for ID:", myid, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Extract segmentation path for K segments (this may return a non-atomic object)
  fp <- findpath(seg, K)
  
  # Convert to an atomic vector before sorting:
  bp <- sort(unlist(fp))
  
  # Assign segment numbers based on the breakpoints.
  seg_num <- rep(NA, nrow(subset_data))
  current_seg <- 1
  start_idx <- 1
  for(b in bp) {
    seg_num[start_idx:b] <- current_seg
    current_seg <- current_seg + 1
    start_idx <- b + 1
  }
  if(start_idx <= nrow(subset_data)) {
    seg_num[start_idx:nrow(subset_data)] <- current_seg
  }
  subset_data$segment <- seg_num
  
  # Split data by segment and classify each segment:
  segments <- split(subset_data, subset_data$segment)
  seg_classes <- sapply(segments, classify_segment)
  
  # Map classification back to the data:
  subset_data <- subset_data %>%
    mutate(behavior = as.character(NA))
  for(seg in names(segments)) {
    subset_data$behavior[subset_data$segment == seg] <- seg_classes[[seg]]
  }
  
  # Convert behavior to factor with desired order:
  subset_data$behavior <- factor(subset_data$behavior, 
                                 levels = c("Resident", "Nomadism", "Dispersal", "Migration", 
                                            "Partial Migration", "Facultative Migration", "Mixed Migration"))
  
  list(
    id = myid,
    segmentation = bp,
    data = subset_data,
    classes = seg_classes
  )
}

# Process all IDs using purrr::map:
results <- map(ids, process_id)
results <- compact(results)

# Example: Plot segmentation and classification for the first ID
if(length(results) > 0) {
  id1 <- results[[1]]
  
  # Plot R2n over time colored by behavior:
  p_time <- ggplot(id1$data, aes(x = date, y = R2n, color = behavior)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_line() +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("R2n Over Time for ID", id1$id, "with Behavior Classification"),
         x = "Date",
         y = "R2n",
         color = "Behavior")
  print(p_time)
  
  # Plot spatial trajectory colored by behavior (assuming x and y exist):
  p_space <- ggplot(id1$data, aes(x = x, y = y, color = behavior)) +
    geom_path(alpha = 0.8, size = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Movement Trajectory for ID", id1$id, "with Behavior Classification"),
         x = "X Coordinate",
         y = "Y Coordinate",
         color = "Behavior")
  print(p_space)
}


```

## Processing Batching of Migratory Animals 

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)

# Define list of Migratory IDs
migratory_ids <- c(100, 119, 12, 15, 18, 33, 34, 36, 38, 41, 42, 43,
                   51, 57, 61, 64, 66, 78, 79, 99, 30, 24, 25, 35)

# Define base path to your CSV files
base_path <- "<LOCAL_PATH>"

# Columns to be removed
columns_to_remove <- c("x_2", "id_2", "mean_r2n", "median_r2n", "sd_r2n", "min_r2n", "max_r2n",
                       "mean_dist", "median_dist", "sd_dist", "min_dist", "max_dist", "x_1",
                       "r2n_p25", "r2n_p50", "r2n_p75", "r2n_p90", "r2n_p95",
                       "x_2_2", "dist_p25", "dist_p50", "dist_p75", "dist_p90", "dist_p95")

# Loop through each ID
for (id in migratory_ids) {
  
  # Construct file path
  file_name <- paste0("Testing_ID", id, ".csv")
  file_path <- file.path(base_path, file_name)
  
  # Read in the data
  deer_data <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  # Clean column names
  deer_data <- clean_names(deer_data)
  
  # --- Process migration_status ---
  if ("migration_status" %in% names(deer_data)) {
    deer_data$migration_status <- gsub("Transition to Migratory", "Migratory", deer_data$migration_status)
  }

  # --- Create or overwrite movement_behavior column ---
  if (!"movement_behavior" %in% names(deer_data)) {
    deer_data$movement_behavior <- if ("migration_status" %in% names(deer_data)) {
      deer_data$migration_status
    } else {
      NA
    }
  }

  # --- Relabel transitions within movement_behavior (preserve original values first) ---
  behavior <- deer_data$movement_behavior
  
  # Step 1: Identify first Migratory and relabel to "Transition to Migratory"
  first_migratory_idx <- which(behavior == "Migratory")[1]
  if (!is.na(first_migratory_idx)) {
    deer_data$movement_behavior[first_migratory_idx] <- "Transition to Migratory"
  }

  # Step 2: Identify first Resident after a Migratory block and relabel to "Transition to Resident"
  if (!is.na(first_migratory_idx)) {
    resident_after_migratory_idx <- which(behavior == "Resident" & seq_along(behavior) > first_migratory_idx)[1]
    if (!is.na(resident_after_migratory_idx)) {
      deer_data$movement_behavior[resident_after_migratory_idx] <- "Transition to Resident"
    }
  }

  # --- Add special_behavior column if missing ---
  if (!"special_behavior" %in% names(deer_data)) {
    deer_data$special_behavior <- 0
  }

  # --- Remove unwanted columns if they exist ---
  deer_data <- deer_data %>% select(-any_of(columns_to_remove))

  # Save updated CSV
  write.csv(deer_data, file = file_path, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("Updated and cleaned:", file_name, "\n")
}

```

## Combining CSVs into Migratory and Resident classification to perform EDA

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)

# Define ID groups
migratory_ids <- c(100, 119, 12, 15, 18, 33, 34, 36, 38, 41, 42, 43, 51, 57, 61, 64, 66, 78, 79, 99, 30, 24, 25, 35,
                   107, 111, 16, 76, 13, 17, 21, 50, 7, 67, 60, 124, 40, 65, 91, 23, 44)

resident_ids <- c(104, 105, 108, 109, 113, 114, 115, 116, 118, 120, 121, 122, 125, 129, 130, 141, 19, 20, 29, 3, 37, 46,
                  47, 48, 53, 55, 56, 58, 6, 62, 68, 69, 70, 71, 73, 74, 77, 8, 80, 81, 82, 83, 84, 88, 89, 9, 90, 92,
                  93, 94, 96, 31, 32, 45, 102, 11, 14, 22, 26, 27, 32, 5, 95, 1, 2, 4, 72)

# Base path
base_path <- "<LOCAL_PATH>"

# Columns to be removed - lowercase version after clean_names()
columns_to_remove <- c("mean_r2n", "median_r2n", "sd_r2n", "min_r2n", "max_r2n", 
                       "mean_dist", "median_dist", "sd_dist", "min_dist", "max_dist",
                       "r2n_p25", "r2n_p50", "r2n_p75", "r2n_p90", "r2n_p95",
                       "dist_p25", "dist_p50", "dist_p75", "dist_p90", "dist_p95", 
                       "id_2")  # Second ID column only

# Initialize empty dataframes
combined_migratory <- data.frame()
combined_resident  <- data.frame()

# Function to read, clean, drop extra columns and bind
safe_read_and_bind <- function(ids, target_df) {
  for (id in ids) {
    file_path <- file.path(base_path, paste0("Testing_ID", id, ".csv"))
    
    if (file.exists(file_path)) {
      temp_data <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      
      # Clean column names
      temp_data <- temp_data %>% clean_names()
      
      # Drop unwanted columns if present
      cols_to_drop <- intersect(columns_to_remove, colnames(temp_data))
      if (length(cols_to_drop) > 0) {
        temp_data <- temp_data %>% select(-all_of(cols_to_drop))
      }
      
      # Ensure only *one* ID column remains
      if (!"id" %in% colnames(temp_data)) {
        temp_data$id <- id
      } else {
        temp_data$id <- as.character(temp_data$id)
      }

      # Bind to combined dataframe
      target_df <- bind_rows(target_df, temp_data)
      
    } else {
      cat("⚠️ File missing for ID:", id, "\n")
    }
  }
  return(target_df)
}

# Apply to both groups
combined_migratory <- safe_read_and_bind(migratory_ids, combined_migratory)
combined_resident  <- safe_read_and_bind(resident_ids,  combined_resident)

# Export cleaned combined files
write.csv(combined_migratory, file = file.path(base_path, "all_migratory_combined.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(combined_resident,  file = file.path(base_path, "all_resident_combined.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)

cat("✅ All combined and cleaned successfully!\n")
```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)

# Load migratory dataset

  clean_names()

# Convert datetime column correctly
migratory_data$date_time <- as.POSIXct(migratory_data$date_time, format = "%m/%d/%y %H:%M", tz = "UTC")

# Ensure date_time is properly parsed
migratory_data <- migratory_data %>%
  mutate(date_time = as.POSIXct(date_time, format = "%m/%d/%y %H:%M", tz = "UTC"))


# Extract proper date directly from parsed date_time
migratory_data$date <- as.Date(migratory_data$date_time)

# Update season classification based on paper definition
migratory_data$season <- case_when(
  (month(migratory_data$date) >= 5 & month(migratory_data$date) <= 10) ~ "Summer",
  TRUE ~ "Winter"
)



# -------------------- EDA SECTION ----------------------

# 1. Summary of data structure
glimpse(migratory_data)

# 2. Fix count per animal ID

  count(id, name = "n_fixes") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_fixes))

summary(migratory_data$dist)

  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "darkorange", color = "black") +

  theme_minimal()

  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Movement Over Time", x = "Time", y = "Distance Moved") +
  theme_minimal()

# 7. Number of fixes by season
ggplot(migratory_data, aes(x = season)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "Fix Count by Season", x = "Season", y = "Number of Fixes") +
  theme_minimal()

# 8. Movement Behavior breakdown
ggplot(migratory_data, aes(x = migration_status)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "purple") +
  labs(title = "Migration Status Breakdown", x = "Behavior", y = "Fix Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# 9. Spatial distribution (Longitude vs Latitude)
ggplot(migratory_data, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Spatial Distribution of Fixes", x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# 10. Heatmap of Fix Density
```

## EDA on New Resident Dataset

```{r}

# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
library(viridis)
library(patchwork)

# Load the resident dataset
resident_data <- read.csv("<LOCAL_PATH>", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  clean_names()

# Parse datetime properly
resident_data$date_time <- as.POSIXct(resident_data$date_time, format = "%m/%d/%y %H:%M", tz = "UTC")

library(lubridate)

# Ensure date_time is properly parsed
resident_data <- resident_data %>%
  mutate(date_time = as.POSIXct(date_time, format = "%m/%d/%y %H:%M", tz = "UTC"))


# Extract clean date column
resident_data$date <- as.Date(resident_data$date_time)

# Update season classification based on paper definition
resident_data$season <- case_when(
  (month(resident_data$date) >= 5 & month(resident_data$date) <= 10) ~ "Summer",
  TRUE ~ "Winter"
)

# Ensure that the migration status column is clean
# Clean up movement_behavior column — force all to "Resident"
resident_data$migration_status <- "Resident"

# --------------------- EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS ----------------------

# 1. Dataset structure
glimpse(resident_data)

# 2. Number of fixes per ID
fix_counts_resident <- resident_data %>%
  count(id, name = "n_fixes") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_fixes))

print(fix_counts_resident)

# 3. Distance summary stats
summary(resident_data$dist)

# 4. Histogram of movement distances
ggplot(resident_data, aes(x = dist)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100, fill = "steelblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Distance per Fix (Resident)", x = "Distance (meters)", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

# Double check the temporal ping intervals. (Make sure it is regularized / skipping GPS pings)

# 5. Relative turning angle distribution
ggplot(resident_data, aes(x = rel_angle)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "darkorange", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Relative Turning Angle Distribution (Resident)", x = "Relative Angle (radians)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# 6. Movement over time per ID
ggplot(resident_data, aes(x = date_time, y = dist, group = id, color = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Movement Over Time by Individual", x = "Time", y = "Distance") +
  theme_minimal()

# 7. Fix counts by season
ggplot(resident_data, aes(x = season)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "Fix Count by Season (Resident)", x = "Season", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# 8. Migration Status behavior breakdown
ggplot(resident_data, aes(x = migration_status)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "purple") +
  labs(title = "Migratoin Status Distribution (Resident)", x = "Behavior", y = "Fix Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# 9. Spatial distribution (map)
ggplot(resident_data, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Spatial Distribution of Resident Fixes", x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# 10. Density heatmap (UTM)
ggplot(resident_data, aes(x = utm_easting, y = utm_northing)) +
  stat_density2d(aes(fill = ..density..), geom = "raster", contour = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis() +
  labs(title = "Fix Density Heatmap (Resident)", x = "UTM Easting", y = "UTM Northing") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Flagging pings and distances that are beyong 5000 meteres per 4 hours and Removing unrealistic movements

```{r}

## --- Preprocessing: Order data and compute time differences ---
resident_data <- resident_data %>%
  arrange(id, date_time) %>% # Order by ID and time
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(time_diff_hr = as.numeric(difftime(date_time, lag(date_time), units = "hours"))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(time_diff_hr = if_else(time_diff_hr == 0, NA_real_, time_diff_hr))  # Replace zero gaps with NA

## --- Create Threshold Flags ---
resident_data <- resident_data %>%
  mutate(
    suspect_jump = ifelse(dist > 5000 & time_diff_hr > 4, 1, 0),
    extreme_jump = ifelse(dist > 9000, 1, 0)
  )

## --- Visualize Flagged Points ---
ggplot(resident_data, aes(x = time_diff_hr, y = dist, color = as.factor(suspect_jump))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "gray", "1" = "red")) +
  labs(title = "Flagged Long-Distance Fixes with Large Time Gaps",
       color = "Suspect Jump",
       x = "Time Difference (hours, log scale)",
       y = "Distance (meters, log scale)") +
  theme_minimal()

## --- Extract IDs with suspect jumps ---
flagged_ids <- resident_data %>%
  filter(suspect_jump == 1) %>%
  distinct(id) %>%
  arrange(id)
print(flagged_ids)

## --- Convert IDs to Vector for Further Analysis ---
flagged_vector <- flagged_ids$id

## --- Check Temporal Structure for Flagged Points ---
resident_data %>%
  filter(id %in% flagged_vector, suspect_jump == 1) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    max_time_gap = max(time_diff_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_dist = max(dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flags = n()
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_flags))

resident_data %>%
  filter(id %in% flagged_vector, suspect_jump == 1) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_flags = n(),
    max_time_gap = max(time_diff_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_time_gap = median(time_diff_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_dist = max(dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_dist = median(dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_speed = median(dist / time_diff_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_speed = max(dist / time_diff_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
    time_gap_gt_6hr = any(time_diff_hr > 6, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_flags))

## --- Step 1: Identify Flagged Points with Maximum Distance or Time Gap ---
flagged_points <- resident_data %>%
  filter(suspect_jump == 1, !is.na(dist), !is.na(time_diff_hr)) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    is_max_dist = dist == max(dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_max_gap = time_diff_hr == max(time_diff_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
    alignment = case_when(
      is_max_dist & is_max_gap ~ "Both Max Distance & Gap",
      is_max_dist ~ "Max Distance Only",
      is_max_gap ~ "Max Time Gap Only",
      TRUE ~ "Other Flagged Point"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(id, date_time, dist, time_diff_hr, is_max_dist, is_max_gap, alignment)


## --- Step 2: Display Meaningful Flagged Points ---
flagged_points %>%
  filter(alignment != "Other Flagged Point") %>%
  arrange(id, desc(dist)) %>%
  print(n = 32)

## --- Removing Unrealistic Movements ---
# Recalculate speed (distance per hour)
resident_data <- resident_data %>%
  mutate(dist_per_hr = dist / time_diff_hr)

# Define unrealistic movement conditions (flag if distance > 8000 OR speed > 1300 m/hr)
unrealistic_points <- resident_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(dist), !is.na(time_diff_hr)) %>%
  filter(dist > 8000 | dist_per_hr > 1300)

print(unrealistic_points)
colnames(unrealistic_points)

# Save IDs and times for traceability
unrealistic_summary <- unrealistic_points %>%
  dplyr::select(id, date_time, dist, time_diff_hr, dist_per_hr)

print(unrealistic_summary)

# Create a cleaned dataset by removing unrealistic points
resident_cleaned <- resident_data %>%
  anti_join(unrealistic_summary, by = c("id", "date_time"))

## --- Visualize Cleaned Data ---
ggplot(resident_cleaned, aes(x = time_diff_hr, y = dist)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "steelblue") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Cleaned Distance vs Time Gap Between Fixes (log scale)",
       x = "Time Difference (hours, log scale)",
       y = "Distance (meters, log scale)") +
  theme_minimal()


colnames(resident_cleaned)
```

```{r}
## --- Step 1: Identify Flagged Points with Maximum Distance or Time Gap ---

  filter(suspect_jump == 1, !is.na(dist), !is.na(time_diff_hr)) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    is_max_dist = dist == max(dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_max_gap = time_diff_hr == max(time_diff_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
    alignment = case_when(
      is_max_dist & is_max_gap ~ "Both Max Distance & Gap",
      is_max_dist ~ "Max Distance Only",
      is_max_gap ~ "Max Time Gap Only",
      TRUE ~ "Other Flagged Point"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(id, date_time, dist, time_diff_hr, is_max_dist, is_max_gap, alignment)

## --- Step 2: Display Meaningful Flagged Points ---
flagged_points_migratory %>%
  filter(alignment != "Other Flagged Point") %>%
  arrange(id, desc(dist)) %>%
  print(n = 90)

## --- Removing Unrealistic Movements ---
# Recalculate speed (distance per hour)
migratory_data <- migratory_data %>%
  mutate(dist_per_hr = dist / time_diff_hr)

# Define unrealistic movement conditions (flag if distance > 8000 OR speed > 1300 m/hr)
unrealistic_points_migratory <- migratory_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(dist), !is.na(time_diff_hr)) %>%
  filter(dist > 8000 | dist_per_hr > 1300)

print(unrealistic_points_migratory)
colnames(unrealistic_points_migratory)

# Save IDs and times for traceability
unrealistic_summary_migratory <- unrealistic_points_migratory %>%
  dplyr::select(id, date_time, dist, time_diff_hr, dist_per_hr)
print(unrealistic_summary_migratory)

# Create a cleaned dataset by removing unrealistic points
migratory_cleaned <- migratory_data %>%
  anti_join(unrealistic_summary_migratory, by = c("id", "date_time"))

## --- Visualize Cleaned Data ---
ggplot(migratory_cleaned, aes(x = time_diff_hr, y = dist)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "steelblue") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Cleaned Distance vs Time Gap Between Fixes (Migratory, log scale)",
       x = "Time Difference (hours, log scale)",
       y = "Distance (meters, log scale)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Check dispersal 
```{r}
## --- Suspected Dispersal Data: Preprocessing ---
dispersal_ids <- c(102, 11, 14, 22, 26, 27, 32, 5, 95)

dispersal_data <- migratory_data %>% 
  filter(id %in% dispersal_ids) %>%
  arrange(id, date_time) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(time_diff_hr = as.numeric(difftime(date_time, lag(date_time), units = "hours"))) %>%
  ungroup()



# Calculate displacement
dispersal_data <- dispersal_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(date_time) %>%
  mutate(
    start_easting = first(utm_easting),
    start_northing = first(utm_northing),
    displacement = sqrt((utm_easting - start_easting)^2 + (utm_northing - start_northing)^2)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# 1. Spatial Trajectory Plot
ggplot(dispersal_data, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, group = id, color = factor(id))) +
  geom_path(size = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Dispersal Trajectories",
       x = "Longitude",
       y = "Latitude",
       color = "ID") +
  theme_minimal()

# 1. Subset Spatial Trajectory Plot
ggplot(subset(dispersal_data, id == 95), aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, group = id, color = factor(id))) +
  geom_path(size = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Dispersal Trajectories",
       x = "Longitude",
       y = "Latitude",
       color = "ID") +
  theme_minimal()

# Flag 5 and 22 -105.7 any locations less than that, but more than -106 as dispersal. (DONE)
# 102 anything left of -105.67 as resident and anything right of that is dispersal. (DONE)
# ID 11 below of latitude 42.65 resident above above is dispersal. (DONE)
# ID 26 anything left of -105.72 is resident and above is dispersal. (DONE)
# ID 27 anything left of -105.7 is resident
# ID 95 is full dispersal. (DONE)
# ID 32 is full dispersal. (DONE)



# 2. Displacement Over Time
ggplot(dispersal_data, aes(x = date_time, y = displacement, color = factor(id))) +
  geom_line(size = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Net Displacement Over Time",
       x = "Date/Time",
       y = "Displacement from Start (meters)",
       color = "ID") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Optionally label extreme displacements
extreme_disp <- dispersal_data %>% 
  group_by(id) %>% 
  filter(displacement == max(displacement, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup()

ggplot(dispersal_data, aes(x = date_time, y = displacement, color = factor(id))) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text_repel(data = extreme_disp, aes(label = id), size = 3, color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Net Displacement Over Time (Extreme Points Labeled)",
       x = "Date/Time",
       y = "Displacement (meters)",
       color = "ID") +
  theme_minimal()

# 3. Movement Metrics Summary
dispersal_summary <- dispersal_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    total_distance = sum(dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_displacement = max(displacement, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_speed = median(dist_per_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_points = n()
  )
print(dispersal_summary)

```

```{r}
# Create a function to plot 1 phase at at time for better movement understanding
library(data.table)
library(ggrepel)

location_plot_static_phase <- function(deer_data, desired_phase, phase_colors = NULL) {
  # Set default colors if not provided
  if (is.null(phase_colors)) {
    phase_colors <- c("Remove" = "black", 
                      desired_phase = "blue")
  }
  
  # Convert the data to a data.table to use rleid()
  dt <- as.data.table(deer_data)
  dt[, phase_grp := rleid(phases)]
  
  # Identify the contiguous groups that contain the desired phase
  desired_groups <- unique(dt[phases == desired_phase, phase_grp])
  if (length(desired_groups) == 0) {
    stop("No rows with the desired phase were found.")
  }
  
  # For simplicity, choose the first occurrence (lowest phase_grp value)
  target_grp <- min(desired_groups)
  groups_to_plot <- target_grp
  
  # Check if the immediately preceding group is "Remove"
  if (target_grp > 1) {
    prev_phase <- dt[phase_grp == (target_grp - 1), unique(phases)]
    if (prev_phase == "Remove") {
      groups_to_plot <- c(target_grp - 1, target_grp)
    }
  }
  
  # Filter the data for only those groups
  plot_data <- dt[phase_grp %in% groups_to_plot]
  plot_data <- as.data.frame(plot_data)
  
  # Force the phases column to be a factor with only the desired levels
  plot_data$phases <- factor(plot_data$phases, levels = c("Remove", desired_phase))
  
  # Create the plot
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = phases)) +
    geom_path(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Movement of Deer ID:", unique(deer_data$id),
                       "\nPhase:", desired_phase, "and associated Remove"),
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude",
         color = "Phase") +
    scale_color_manual(values = phase_colors)
}
```

```{r}
## Recalculate the dx dy and rel_angle - Residents

resident_data <- resident_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%                      # Process each deer separately
  arrange(date_time) %>%                # Order fixes chronologically
  mutate(
    # Calculate differences between consecutive fixes
    dx = utm_easting - lag(utm_easting),
    dy = utm_northing - lag(utm_northing),
    # Calculate the absolute angle (in degrees) for each movement vector;
    # The first observation in each group will be NA.
    abs_angle = atan2(dy, dx) * 180 / pi,
    # Calculate the relative (turning) angle between consecutive movement vectors.
    # The turning angle is the difference in consecutive absolute angles.
    # We adjust it to be within [-180, 180] degrees.
    rel_angle = (((abs_angle - lag(abs_angle)) + 180) %% 360) - 180
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Zoo package has rollapply function. ( ?zoo::rollapply) Create a loop to go throught over every ID. break for Migratory to include summer and winter ranges. keep them separate. Do not apply NA values, Align so it is center point So it is calculating the previous week up to that point. 

# Make sure it is 7 days not 7 temporal points.

# For each id, compute the 7-day moving average of dist using a time-based window - Residents
resident_data <- resident_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(date_time) %>%
  mutate(
    avg_7day_dist_zoo = {
      # Create a zoo object with date_time as index
      z <- zoo(dist, date_time)
      # Get the time index (POSIXct)
      times <- index(z)
      # For each observation, determine how many observations fall within the past 7 days:
      widths <- sapply(seq_along(times), function(i) {
        # Find indices where time is within (current time - 7 days) to current time
        valid_idx <- which(times >= times[i] - as.difftime(7, units = "days") & times <= times[i])
        # Window width is the number of such observations
        length(valid_idx)
      })
      # Now apply a rolling mean with the custom widths
      # rollapplyr will use each corresponding width to take the last 'width[i]' observations.
      roll_mean <- rollapplyr(z, width = widths, FUN = mean, partial = TRUE, align = "right")
      coredata(roll_mean)
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup()



# For each id, compute the 7-day moving average of dist using a time-based window - Migratory

# Calculate sinuosity on 7-day moving window - Resident 
calc_sinuosity <- function(east, north, dist) {
  # Require at least two observations to compute a meaningful value
  if(length(east) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  
  # Net displacement: Euclidean distance from first to last observation
  net_disp <- sqrt((east[length(east)] - east[1])^2 +
                   (north[length(north)] - north[1])^2)
  
  # Total distance traveled in the window
  tot <- sum(dist, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Avoid division by zero
  if(tot == 0) return(NA_real_)
  
  # Sinuosity as net displacement divided by total distance traveled
  net_disp / tot
}


# Calculate sinuosity on 7-day moving window - Migratory
calc_sinuosity <- function(east, north, dist) {
  # Require at least two observations to compute a meaningful value
  if(length(east) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  
  # Net displacement: Euclidean distance from first to last observation
  net_disp <- sqrt((east[length(east)] - east[1])^2 +
                   (north[length(north)] - north[1])^2)
  
  # Total distance traveled in the window
  tot <- sum(dist, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Avoid division by zero
  if(tot == 0) return(NA_real_)
  
  # Sinuosity as net displacement divided by total distance traveled
  net_disp / tot
}


# Apply function
resident_data <- resident_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(date_time) %>%
  mutate(rolling_sinuosity = slide_index_dbl(
    .x = row_number(),    # Dummy variable; we'll use the index to subset the window
    .i = date_time,       # Use the date_time as the time index
    .f = function(idx) {
      # For the current window defined by idx,
      # compute sinuosity using the corresponding UTM and distance values
      calc_sinuosity(utm_easting[idx], utm_northing[idx], dist[idx])
    },
    .before = days(7),    # Include fixes from the previous 7 days
    .after = 0,           # Include up to the current observation
    .complete = FALSE     # Compute even if the full 7-day window isn't available
  )) %>%
  ungroup()

    .after = 0,           # Include up to the current observation

  )) %>%

    # Calculate the relative (turning) angle between consecutive movement vectors.
    # The turning angle is the difference in consecutive absolute angles.
    # We adjust it to be within [-180, 180] degrees.
    rel_angle = (((abs_angle - lag(abs_angle)) + 180) %% 360) - 180
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Keep an eye out for rel_angle
# Take the absolute value of rel_angle
updated_migratory_data_4 <- updated_migratory_data_4 %>% dplyr::mutate(abs_rel_angle = abs(rel_angle))

# For each id, compute the 7-day moving average of dist using a time-based window - Migratory
updated_migratory_data_4 <- updated_migratory_data_4 %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(date_time) %>%
  mutate(
    avg_7day_dist_zoo = {
      # Create a zoo object with date_time as index
      z <- zoo(dist, date_time)
      # Get the time index (POSIXct)
      times <- index(z)
      # For each observation, determine how many observations fall within the past 7 days:
      widths <- sapply(seq_along(times), function(i) {
        # Find indices where time is within (current time - 7 days) to current time
        valid_idx <- which(times >= times[i] - as.difftime(7, units = "days") & times <= times[i])
        # Window width is the number of such observations
        length(valid_idx)
      })
      # Now apply a rolling mean with the custom widths
      # rollapplyr will use each corresponding width to take the last 'width[i]' observations.
      roll_mean <- rollapplyr(z, width = widths, FUN = mean, partial = TRUE, align = "right")
      coredata(roll_mean)
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup()



# sinuosity = R2n / sum(dist) in total - Migratory 

ordered_dups_sinuosity <- updated_migratory_data_4 %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(date_time) %>%
  summarise(
    total_distance = sum(dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    net_displacement = sqrt((last(utm_easting) - first(utm_easting))^2 +
                              (last(utm_northing) - first(utm_northing))^2),
    sinuosity = net_displacement / total_distance
  )
print(migratory_sinuosity)


# Calculate sinuosity on 7-day moving window - Migratory
calc_sinuosity <- function(east, north, dist) {
  # Require at least two observations to compute a meaningful value
  if(length(east) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  
  # Net displacement: Euclidean distance from first to last observation
  net_disp <- sqrt((east[length(east)] - east[1])^2 +
                   (north[length(north)] - north[1])^2)
  
  # Total distance traveled in the window
  tot <- sum(dist, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Avoid division by zero
  if(tot == 0) return(NA_real_)
  
  # Sinuosity as net displacement divided by total distance traveled
  net_disp / tot
}


# Apply function - migratory
updated_migratory_data_4 <- updated_migratory_data_4 %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(date_time) %>%
  mutate(rolling_sinuosity = slide_index_dbl(
    .x = row_number(),    # Dummy variable; we'll use the index to subset the window
    .i = date_time,       # Use the date_time as the time index
    .f = function(idx) {
      # For the current window defined by idx,
      # compute sinuosity using the corresponding UTM and distance values
      calc_sinuosity(utm_easting[idx], utm_northing[idx], dist[idx])
    },
    .before = days(7),    # Include fixes from the previous 7 days
    .after = 0,           # Include up to the current observation
    .complete = FALSE     # Compute even if the full 7-day window isn't available
  )) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Fitting Dynamic Brownian Bridge Movement Model
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(move)
library(raster)
library(sp)
library(lubridate)

## --- 1. Filter out Non-Resident Behaviors
resident_data <- resident_data %>%
  filter(!movement_behavior %in% c("Transition to RangeShift", "RangeShift"))

## --- 2. Ensure date_time is POSIXct
# Ensure that date_time is in the proper format
resident_data$date_time <- parse_date_time(resident_data$date_time, 
                                                      orders = c("Y-m-d H:M:S", "Y-m-d", "mdy HM", "mdy"),
                                                      tz = "UTC")

## --- 2.5 Remove Large Time Gaps (> 50 hours)
resident_data_filtered <- resident_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(date_time) %>%
  mutate(time_diff_hr = as.numeric(difftime(date_time, lag(date_time), units = "hours"))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(is.na(time_diff_hr) | time_diff_hr <= 150)

## --- 3. Split Data by ID ---
split_residents <- split(resident_data_filtered, resident_data_filtered$id)

## --- 4. Pre-screen: Minimum Fix Count (>=50) and Sufficient Spatial Spread (>500m in both directions)
split_residents <- split_residents[
  sapply(split_residents, function(df) {
    nrow(df) >= 0 &&
      (max(df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE) - min(df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE)) > 500 &&
      (max(df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE) - min(df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE)) > 500
  })
]

## --- 5. Fit dBBMM for Each Resident ---
bbmm_results <- list()

for (id in names(split_residents)) {
  df <- split_residents[[id]]
  df <- df %>% arrange(date_time)
  
  # Remove duplicated timestamps
  df <- df[!duplicated(df$date_time), ]
  
  # Create move object
  m <- move(x = df$utm_easting,
            y = df$utm_northing,
            time = df$date_time,
            data = df,
            proj = CRS("+proj=utm +zone=12 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"),
            animal = as.character(df$id[1]))
  
  # Calculate spatial spread in both directions
  spread_x <- max(df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE) - min(df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE)
  spread_y <- max(df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE) - min(df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Set fixed buffer: default = 10,000 m but for ID "45", use 30,000 m
  fixed_buffer <- if (id == "45") 30000 else 10000
  
  # Calculate dynamic buffer (half of the spread) plus the fixed buffer
  buffer_x <- max(10000, spread_x * 0.5) + fixed_buffer
  buffer_y <- max(10000, spread_y * 0.5) + fixed_buffer
  
  # Create buffered extent
  e <- extent(min(df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE) - buffer_x,
              max(df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer_x,
              min(df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE) - buffer_y,
              max(df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer_y)
  
  # Create raster grid with 100 m resolution
  r <- raster(e, res = 100)
  crs(r) <- CRS("+proj=utm +zone=12 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs")
  
  # Fit dBBMM using dynamic buffer with error handling
  cat("➡ Fitting dBBMM for ID:", id, "\n")
  bb <- tryCatch({
    brownian.bridge.dyn(m,
                        raster = r,
                        location.error = 20,
                        window.size = 31,
                        margin = 11)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("❌ Failed for ID:", id, "—", e$message, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if (!is.null(bb)) {
    bbmm_results[[id]] <- bb
  }
}


cat("✅ dBBMM Fitting for Migratory Residents Completed. Total:", length(bbmm_results), "\n")

```

```{r}
## --- DBBMMBurstStack: Time-Resolved UDs (Per Day) with Progress Bar ---

library(dplyr)
library(move)
library(raster)
library(sp)
library(lubridate)

bbmm_burst_results <- list()

# Progress bar setup
pb <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = length(split_residents), style = 3)
counter <- 0

for (id in names(split_residents)) {
  counter <- counter + 1
  setTxtProgressBar(pb, counter)

  df <- split_residents[[id]] %>% arrange(date_time)
  df <- df[!duplicated(df$date_time), ]

  # Create move object
  m <- move(x = df$utm_easting,
            y = df$utm_northing,
            time = df$date_time,
            data = df,
            proj = CRS("+proj=utm +zone=12 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"),
            animal = id)

  # Assign burst IDs using 1-day intervals
  burst_ids <- cut(df$date_time[-1], breaks = "4 hours", labels = FALSE)
  mb <- burst(m, as.character(burst_ids))
  burst_n <- length(unique(burst_ids))

  cat(sprintf("\n🌀 Fitting dBBMMBurstStack for ID: %s | %d bursts | %s\n", id, burst_n, Sys.time()))

  # Calculate bounding box with dynamic + fixed buffer
  min_x <- min(df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_x <- max(df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE)
  min_y <- min(df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_y <- max(df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE)

  spread_x <- max_x - min_x
  spread_y <- max_y - min_y

  fixed_buffer <- case_when(
    id == "45" ~ 50000,
    id == "37" ~ 50000,
    id == "72" ~ 50000,
    TRUE ~ 10000
  )

  buffer_x <- max(10000, spread_x * 0.5) + fixed_buffer
  buffer_y <- max(10000, spread_y * 0.5) + fixed_buffer

  bbox_vals <- c(min_x - buffer_x,
                 max_x + buffer_x,
                 min_y - buffer_y,
                 max_y + buffer_y)

  # Fit DBBMMBurstStack with error handling
  bb_burst <- tryCatch({
    brownian.bridge.dyn(mb,
                        dimSize = 500,
                        bbox = bbox_vals,
                        ext = 5.5,
                        location.error = 20,
                        window.size = 31,
                        margin = 11,
                        time.step = 5)  # limit integration resolution (faster + safer)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("❌ BurstStack failed for ID:", id, "—", e$message, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  })

  if (!is.null(bb_burst)) {
    bbmm_burst_results[[id]] <- bb_burst
  }
}

close(pb)
cat("✅ Finished fitting DBBMMBurstStack models. Total:", length(bbmm_burst_results), "\n")
```

```{r}
library(raster)
library(sp)

# --- 1. Extract space‐use for one burst object ----
extract_space_use <- function(bb, id) {
  # coerce the SpatialGridDataFrame into a RasterStack
  ud_stack <- raster::stack(bb)
  
  # get the burst times
  burst_times <- bb@DBMvar@means
  # only as many times as there are layers
  times <- burst_times[1:nlayers(ud_stack)]
  
  # count non‐zero cells in each layer
  spaces <- vapply(
    seq_len(nlayers(ud_stack)),
    function(i) sum(raster::values(ud_stack[[i]]) > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    integer(1)
  )
  
  # return a data.frame with id, time, space_used
  data.frame(
    id         = id,
    time       = as.character(times),
    space_used = spaces,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# --- 2. Loop over all IDs and combine ----
all_ids <- names(bbmm_burst_results)

space_use_list <- lapply(all_ids, function(id) {
  bb <- bbmm_burst_results[[id]]
  extract_space_use(bb, id)
})

space_use_df <- do.call(rbind, space_use_list)
space_use_df <- space_use_df[, c("id", "time", "space_used")]

# --- 3. Write to CSV ----
write.csv(
  space_use_df,
  file = "space_use_all_ids.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

message("✅ Wrote ", nrow(space_use_df), " rows to space_use_all_ids.csv")
```

## Trying AKDE to Resident Dataset
```{r}
## Full AKDE for ALL IDs with multiprocessing & verbose, skipping NULL CI ##

library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(ctmm)
library(lubridate)
library(tibble)
library(zoo)
library(furrr)

# 1) Read & parse resident_data
resident_data <- read.csv(
  "<LOCAL_PATH>",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    date_time = parse_date_time(
      date_time,
      orders = c("Y-m-d H:M:S","Y-m-d","mdy HM","mdy"),
      tz = "UTC"
    )
  )

# 2) Build sf + extract lon/lat
deer_sf <- resident_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude), !is.na(date_time)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326)

ll <- deer_sf %>%
  st_coordinates() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  rename(location.long = X,
         location.lat  = Y)

# 3) Prepare for as.telemetry
dat <- resident_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude), !is.na(date_time)) %>%
  bind_cols(ll) %>%
  select(
    individual.local.identifier = id,
    location.long,
    location.lat,
    timestamp = date_time
  )

# 4) Convert to telemetry list
tel_list <- as.telemetry(
  dat,
  timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
  timezone   = "UTC"
)

# 5) Parallel plan
plan(multisession, workers = parallel::detectCores())
options(future.rng.onMisuse = "ignore")

# 6) Per-ID function
process_id <- function(id) {
  message("🔄 Starting ID ", id)
  tel <- tel_list[[id]]
  
  day_sec  <- 24 * 3600
  week_sec <- 7  * day_sec
  starts   <- tel$t[tel$t <= max(tel$t) - week_sec]
  
  raw_area <- tibble(
    window_start = as.POSIXct(numeric(), origin="1970-01-01", tz="UTC"),
    low          = numeric(),
    est          = numeric(),
    high         = numeric()
  )
  
  for (t0 in starts) {
    message("  → ID ", id, " window @ ", as.POSIXct(t0, origin="1970-01-01", tz="UTC"))
    win <- tel[tel$t >= t0 & tel$t <= (t0 + week_sec), ]
    if (length(win$t) < 20) {
      message("    ↳ only ", length(win$t), " points — skipping")
      next
    }
    
    UD <- tryCatch({
      v0  <- variogram(win, CI="Gauss")
      v2  <- variogram.fit(v0, name="GuessBM", interactive=FALSE)
      m0  <- ctmm.select(win, v2, IC="BIC")
      akde(win, m0, weights=TRUE)
    }, error = function(e) {
      message("    ✖ AKDE error at ", as.POSIXct(t0, origin="1970-01-01", tz="UTC"),
              ": ", e$message)
      NULL
    })
    if (is.null(UD)) next
    
    # --- NEW: safely extract CI table ---
    ci_summary <- tryCatch(summary(UD)$CI, error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(ci_summary)) {
      message("    ⚠ No CI returned for window @ ", as.POSIXct(t0, origin="1970-01-01", tz="UTC"))
      next
    }
    ci_tbl <- as_tibble(ci_summary, rownames = "unit")
    
    area <- ci_tbl %>%
      filter(startsWith(unit, "area")) %>%
      select(low, est, high)
    if (nrow(area) == 0) {
      message("    ⚠ No 'area' row in CI for window @ ", as.POSIXct(t0, origin="1970-01-01", tz="UTC"))
      next
    }
    
    raw_area <- bind_rows(raw_area,
      tibble(
        window_start = as.POSIXct(t0, origin="1970-01-01", tz="UTC"),
        low          = area$low,
        est          = area$est,
        high         = area$high
      )
    )
    message("    ✔ success: est = ", area$est)
  }
  
  message("✅ Completed ID ", id, " (", nrow(raw_area), " windows)")
  raw_area
}

# 7) Run in parallel
all_results <- future_map(
  names(tel_list),
  process_id,
  .progress = TRUE,
  .options  = furrr_options(seed = TRUE)
)

# 8) Combine and inspect
final_df <- bind_rows(all_results)
print(final_df)

print(raw_area)

library(purrr)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}

## Applying Dynamic Brownian Bridge Movement Model to Migratory
library(dplyr)
library(move)
library(raster)
library(sp)
library(lubridate)
library(zoo)

updated_migratory_data_4 <- read.csv("<LOCAL_PATH>", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Ensure that date_time is in the proper format
updated_migratory_data_4$date_time <- parse_date_time(updated_migratory_data_4$date_time, 
                                                      orders = c("Y-m-d H:M:S", "Y-m-d", "mdy HM", "mdy"),
                                                      tz = "UTC")

# Split the migratory_cleaned data by id
split_migrants <- split(updated_migratory_data_4, updated_migratory_data_4$id)

bbmm_migrants_results <- list()

for (id in names(split_migrants)) {
  df <- split_migrants[[id]]
  df <- df %>% arrange(date_time)
  
  # Get the unique phases from the phases column (skip if phase is "Remove")
  unique_phases <- unique(df$phases)
  
  for (phase in unique_phases) {
    if (phase == "Remove") next
    
    sub_df <- df %>% filter(phases == phase)
    
    # Skip if there are fewer than needed fixes for the window (e.g., fewer than 31)
    if (nrow(sub_df) < 31) {
      cat("⚠️ Skipping ID:", id, "Phase:", phase, "- too few fixes (", nrow(sub_df), ") for window.size 21\n")
      next
    }
    
    # Remove duplicate timestamps and rows with missing UTM or date_time values
    sub_df <- sub_df[!duplicated(sub_df$date_time), ]
    sub_df <- sub_df %>% filter(!is.na(utm_easting), !is.na(utm_northing), !is.na(date_time))
    
    if (length(sub_df$utm_easting) != length(sub_df$utm_northing) || 
        length(sub_df$utm_easting) != length(sub_df$date_time)) {
      cat("⚠️ Skipping ID:", id, "Phase:", phase, "- vector length mismatch\n")
      next
    }
    
    # Build the move object
    m <- move(x = sub_df$utm_easting,
              y = sub_df$utm_northing,
              time = sub_df$date_time,
              data = sub_df,
              proj = CRS("+proj=utm +zone=12 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"),
              animal = paste0(id, "_", phase))
    
    # Calculate spatial spread and define buffer distances
    spread_x <- max(sub_df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE) - min(sub_df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE)
    spread_y <- max(sub_df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE) - min(sub_df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE)
    buffer_x <- max(10000, spread_x * 0.5)
    buffer_y <- max(10000, spread_y * 0.5)
    
    # For ID 57 Phase_1, add extra buffers in both x and y directions
    if (id == "57" && phase == "Phase_1") {
      additional_buffer_x <- 30000  # Extra x-buffer (in meters)
      additional_buffer_y <- 30000  # Extra y-buffer (in meters)
      buffer_x <- buffer_x + additional_buffer_x
      buffer_y <- buffer_y + additional_buffer_y
      cat("   ➡ Added extra x-buffer (", additional_buffer_x, "m) and extra y-buffer (", additional_buffer_y, "m) for ID 57 Phase_1\n")
    }
    
    # Create buffered extent and raster
    e <- extent(min(sub_df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE) - buffer_x,
                max(sub_df$utm_easting, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer_x,
                min(sub_df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE) - buffer_y,
                max(sub_df$utm_northing, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer_y)
    r <- raster(e, res = 100)
    crs(r) <- CRS("+proj=utm +zone=12 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs")
    
    # Fit dBBMM with updated window.size (21) and margin (9)
    cat("➡ Fitting dBBMM for ID:", id, "Phase:", phase, "\n")
    bb <- tryCatch({
      brownian.bridge.dyn(m,
                          raster = r,
                          location.error = 20,
                          window.size = 21,
                          margin = 9)
    }, error = function(e) {
      cat("❌ Failed for ID:", id, "Phase:", phase, "-", e$message, "\n")
      return(NULL)
    })
    
    if (!is.null(bb)) {
      bbmm_migrants_results[[paste0(id, "_", phase)]] <- bb
    }
  }
}

cat("✅ dBBMM Fitting for Migratory Residents Completed. Total:", length(bbmm_migrants_results), "\n")

```

```{r}
## --- DBBMMBurstStack for Migratory Data (4-hour bursts) with Progress Bar ---

library(dplyr)
library(move)
library(raster)
library(sp)
library(lubridate)

bbmm_burst_migrants <- list()

# Progress bar over each migrant ID
pb <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = length(split_migrants), style = 3)
counter <- 0

for (id in names(split_migrants)) {
  counter <- counter + 1
  setTxtProgressBar(pb, counter)

  # grab & clean that ID’s points
  df <- split_migrants[[id]] %>%
    arrange(date_time) %>%
    filter(!duplicated(date_time),
           !is.na(utm_easting),
           !is.na(utm_northing))

  # if you want to skip very tiny tracks:
  if (nrow(df) < 10) {
    cat(sprintf("\n⚠️ ID %s has only %d fixes—skipping\n", id, nrow(df)))
    next
  }

  # build a Move object
  m <- move(
    x      = df$utm_easting,
    y      = df$utm_northing,
    time   = df$date_time,
    data   = df,
    proj   = CRS("+proj=utm +zone=12 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"),
    animal = id
  )

  # cut on the *segment* times, i.e. drop the first timestamp so you get length = n_pts - 1
  burst_ids <- cut(df$date_time[-1], breaks = "4 hours", labels = FALSE)
  
  # now burst_ids is length n_pts - 1 and matches the number of segments
  mb <- burst(m, as.character(burst_ids))
  burst_n <- length(unique(burst_ids))

  cat(sprintf("\n🌀 Fitting DBBMMBurstStack for Migrant ID: %s | %d bursts\n",
              id, burst_n))

  # compute bounding box + buffers (tweak as you like)
  min_x <- min(df$utm_easting); max_x <- max(df$utm_easting)
  min_y <- min(df$utm_northing); max_y <- max(df$utm_northing)
  spread_x <- max_x - min_x; spread_y <- max_y - min_y
  fixed_buffer <- 10000  # or use case_when() for special IDs
  buf_x <- max(10000, spread_x * 0.5) + fixed_buffer
  buf_y <- max(10000, spread_y * 0.5) + fixed_buffer

  bbox_vals <- c(
    min_x - buf_x, max_x + buf_x,
    min_y - buf_y, max_y + buf_y
  )

  # fit the dynamic Brownian‐bridge stack
  bb_burst <- tryCatch({
    brownian.bridge.dyn(
      mb,
      dimSize        = 500,
      bbox           = bbox_vals,
      ext            = 5.5,
      location.error = 20,
      window.size    = 31,
      margin         = 11,
      time.step      = 5
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("❌ BurstStack failed for ID %s — %s\n", id, e$message))
    NULL
  })

  if (!is.null(bb_burst)) {
    bbmm_burst_migrants[[id]] <- bb_burst
  }
}

close(pb)
cat(sprintf("\n✅ Finished fitting DBBMMBurstStack for migratory IDs. Total: %d\n",
            length(bbmm_burst_migrants)))


```

## AKDE for Migratory
```{r}
## Sliding‐window AKDE + UD list for Migratory Mule Deer ##

library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(ctmm)
library(lubridate)
library(tibble)
library(zoo)
library(furrr)
library(purrr)

# 1) Read & parse migratory data
migr_data <- read.csv(
  "<LOCAL_PATH>",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    date_time = parse_date_time(
      date_time,
      orders = c("Y-m-d H:M:S","Y-m-d","mdy HM","mdy"),
      tz = "UTC"
    )
  )

# 2) Drop “Remove” and missing, *then* combine id+phase
migr_clean <- migr_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(longitude),
    !is.na(latitude),
    !is.na(date_time),
    phases != "Remove"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    id_phase = paste(id, phases, sep = "_")   # e.g. "42_Phase_1"
  )

# 3) Build sf + extract lon/lat exactly as before
migr_sf <- migr_clean %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326)

migr_ll <- migr_sf %>%
  st_coordinates() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  rename(location.long = X, location.lat = Y)

# 4) Prepare for telemetry – use id_phase as the individual identifier
migr_dat <- migr_clean %>%
  bind_cols(migr_ll) %>%
  select(
    individual.local.identifier = id_phase,
    location.long,
    location.lat,
    timestamp = date_time
  )

migr_tel_list <- as.telemetry(
  migr_dat,
  timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
  timezone   = "UTC"
)

# 5) Parallel plan for migratory pipeline
plan(multisession, workers = parallel::detectCores())
options(future.rng.onMisuse = "ignore")

# 6) Per‐ID function for migratory deer
process_migr_id <- function(deer_id) {
  tel      <- migr_tel_list[[deer_id]]
  day_sec  <- 24 * 3600
  week_sec <- 7  * day_sec
  starts   <- tel$t[tel$t <= max(tel$t) - week_sec]

  raw_area    <- tibble(window_start = POSIXct(), low = numeric(), est = numeric(), high = numeric())
  migr_udList <- list()

  for (t0 in starts) {
    win <- tel[tel$t >= t0 & tel$t <= (t0 + week_sec), ]
    #if (length(win$t) < 20) next

    UD_migr <- tryCatch({
      v0 <- variogram(win, CI="Gauss")
      v2 <- variogram.fit(v0, name="GuessBM", interactive=FALSE)
      m0 <- ctmm.select(win, v2, IC="BIC")
      akde(win, m0, weights=TRUE)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(UD_migr)) next

    # save UD
    migr_udList[[length(migr_udList) + 1]] <- UD_migr

    # extract area CI
    ci <- tryCatch(summary(UD_migr)$CI, error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(ci)) next
    ci_tbl <- as_tibble(ci, rownames="unit")
    a <- ci_tbl %>% filter(startsWith(unit,"area")) %>% select(low, est, high)
    if (nrow(a) == 0) next

    raw_area <- bind_rows(
      raw_area,
      tibble(
        window_start = as.POSIXct(t0, origin="1970-01-01", tz="UTC"),
        low          = a$low,
        est          = a$est,
        high         = a$high
      )
    )
  }

  raw_area <- raw_area %>% mutate(id = deer_id)
  list(area = raw_area, uds = migr_udList)
}

# 7) Run migratory pipeline in parallel
migr_results <- future_map(
  names(migr_tel_list),
  process_migr_id,
  .progress = TRUE,
  .options  = furrr_options(seed = TRUE)
)
names(migr_results) <- names(migr_tel_list)

# 8) Extract the area data frame and the UD list
migr_area_df     <- map2_dfr(migr_results, names(migr_results), ~ .x$area)
migr_ud_list_by_id <- map(migr_results, "uds")

# 9) Verify every (ID, Phase) made it through
orig_migr_ids <- migr_clean %>% 
  distinct(id_phase) %>% 
  pull(id_phase)

done_migr_ids <- migr_area_df %>% 
  distinct(id) %>%      # your area_df’s `id` column holds the id_phase values
  pull(id)

missing_ids <- setdiff(orig_migr_ids, done_migr_ids)

if (length(missing_ids) == 0) {
  message("✅ All migratory ID_Phase combinations processed.")
} else {
  message("⚠️ Missing ID_Phase combos: ", paste(missing_ids, collapse = ", "))
}


library(readr)

# 1) Resident deer
write.csv(
  final_df,
  "<LOCAL_PATH>"
)

# 2) Migratory deer
write.csv(
  migr_area_df,
  "<LOCAL_PATH>"
)
saveRDS(
  migr_ud_list_by_id,
  "<LOCAL_PATH>"
)


colnames(resident_data)
colnames(final_df)

```

# Splitting Winter and Summer Home ranges by average migration start and end date

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(stringr)

# --- Read in and parse date_time properly ---
updated_migratory_data_4 <- read.csv(
  "<LOCAL_PATH>",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    date_time = parse_date_time(
      date_time,
      orders = c("Y-m-d H:M:S","Y-m-d","mdy HM","mdy"),
      tz = "UTC"
    )
  )

# Same for resident_data
resident_data <- read.csv(
  "<LOCAL_PATH>",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    date_time = parse_date_time(
      date_time,
      orders = c("Y-m-d H:M:S","Y-m-d","mdy HM","mdy"),
      tz = "UTC"
    )
  )

# Remove any ID‐phase that is *entirely* “Remove” ---
phases_to_remove <- updated_migratory_data_4 %>%
  group_by(id, phases) %>%
  summarise(all_remove = all(phases == "Remove"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(all_remove) %>%
  select(id, phases)

migratory_no_remove <- updated_migratory_data_4 %>%
  anti_join(phases_to_remove, by = c("id", "phases"))

# --- 2. Label odd‐vs‐even phases ---
migratory_split <- migratory_no_remove %>%
  mutate(
    phase_number = as.numeric(str_replace(phases, "Phase_", "")),
    range_type   = ifelse(phase_number %% 2 == 1,
                          "resident_range",
                          "migratory_range")
  )

# For each id × range_type, take the *end* of that phase
migration_dates_by_type <- migratory_split %>%
  group_by(id, range_type) %>%
  summarise(
    phase_end = max(date_time, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

# Drop in the “standard” month‐day (year = 2000)
migration_dates_by_type <- migration_dates_by_type %>%
  mutate(
    # lubridate::make_date(year, month, day)
    phase_end_std = make_date(
      year  = 2000,
      month = month(phase_end),
      day   = day(phase_end)
    )
  )

# Inspect your result
print(migration_dates_by_type)

# Aggregate: get average and median phase end dates at herd level
herd_migration_summary <- migration_dates_by_type %>%
  group_by(range_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n_ids = n(),
    herd_avg_end_date = as.POSIXct(mean(as.numeric(phase_end_std)) * 86400,
                                   origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
    herd_median_end_date = as.POSIXct(median(as.numeric(phase_end_std)) * 86400,
                                      origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("Herd-level Average End Date<LOCAL_PATH>")
print(herd_migration_summary)


```

## New Season Winter and Summer Definition

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# === Define seasonal boundaries using median end dates ===
winter_start <- as.Date("2000-09-26")  # Winter begins Sep 26
winter_end   <- as.Date("2000-04-20")  # Winter ends Apr 20
# Summer = Apr 21 → Sep 25

# === Function to label season ===
label_season <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      date_std = as.Date(format(date_time, "2000-%m-%d")),  # Normalize to year 2000
      season = case_when(
        date_std >= winter_start | date_std <= winter_end ~ "winter",
        TRUE ~ "summer"
      )
    )
}

# === Apply to full datasets (no need to split anymore) ===
migratory_no_remove <- label_season(migratory_no_remove)
resident_data       <- label_season(resident_data)

# === Optional: check season distribution ===
cat("✅ Migratory seasonal breakdow<LOCAL_PATH>")
print(migratory_no_remove %>% count(season))

cat("✅ Resident seasonal breakdow<LOCAL_PATH>")
print(resident_data %>% count(season))

migratory_no_remove %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(n_phases = n_distinct(phases)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_phases))

migratory_no_remove %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(start_time = min(date_time),
            end_time = max(date_time),
            duration_days = as.numeric(difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "days"))) %>%
  arrange(start_time)
```

## Splitting into data experiments
### 100% CWD Negative - Training and 100% CWD Postive - Testing
```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(slider)


# Define unaffected (CWD-negative) IDs
unaffected_ids <- c(41, 46, 49, 55, 81, 120, # Males
  3, 4, 5, 9, 10, 13, 14, 22, 26, 27, 29, 33, 34, 38, 
  44, 56, 59, 60, 75, 88, 95, 97, 101, 108, 112, 118, 
  123, 129, 7, 42, 43, 45, 50, 51, 66, 76, 77, 78, 
  82, 84, 86, 89, 99, 100, 104, 111, 115, 119, 124, 109 # Females
)

# === Combine all points (resident + migratory w/ migratory points removed) ===
all_data <- bind_rows(resident_data, migratory_no_remove)


# === STEP 2: Combine and label data ===
all_data <- bind_rows(resident_data, migratory_no_remove) %>%
  select(-abs_angle) %>%
  mutate(
    CWD_status = case_when(
      id %in% CWD_Infected_clean ~ "positive",
      id %in% CWD_Free_clean     ~ "negative",
      TRUE                       ~ NA_character_
    ),
    CWD_positive = id %in% CWD_Infected_clean
  )

# === STEP 3: Calculate fixed-window sinuosity ===
calc_windowed_sinuosity <- function(easting, northing) {
  net_disp <- sqrt((easting[length(easting)] - easting[1])^2 +
                   (northing[length(northing)] - northing[1])^2)
  total_dist <- sum(sqrt(diff(easting)^2 + diff(northing)^2), na.rm = TRUE)
  if (total_dist == 0) return(NA_real_)
  net_disp / total_dist
}


# Apply fixed window sinuosity per point
all_data <- all_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(date_time) %>%
  mutate(
    sinuosity_28pt = slide_dbl(
      .x = seq_along(date_time),
      .f = function(idx) {
        calc_windowed_sinuosity(utm_easting[idx], utm_northing[idx])
      },
      .before = 27,
      .after = 0,
      .complete = FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Remove the SD Sinousity for all datasets


# === Create new movement metrics ===

# === STEP 4: Rolling feature metrics including skewness & kurtosis ===
all_data <- all_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  arrange(date_time) %>%
  mutate(
    # abs_rel_angle metrics
    rolling_abs_rel_angle_mean  = slide_dbl(abs_rel_angle, .f = mean,     .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE),
    rolling_abs_rel_angle_var   = slide_dbl(abs_rel_angle, .f = var,      .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE),
    rolling_abs_rel_angle_sd    = slide_dbl(abs_rel_angle, .f = sd,       .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE),
    rolling_abs_rel_angle_skew  = slide_dbl(abs_rel_angle, .f = skewness, .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE),
    rolling_abs_rel_angle_kurt  = slide_dbl(abs_rel_angle, .f = kurtosis, .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE),

    # velocity metrics
    rolling_velo_mean           = slide_dbl(velo,          .f = mean,     .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE),
    rolling_velo_var            = slide_dbl(velo,          .f = var,      .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE),
    rolling_velo_sd             = slide_dbl(velo,          .f = sd,       .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE),
    rolling_velo_skew           = slide_dbl(velo,          .f = skewness, .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE),
    rolling_velo_kurt           = slide_dbl(velo,          .f = kurtosis, .before = 27, .after = 0, .complete = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()



# # Drop abs_angle column
# all_data <- all_data %>%
#   select(-abs_angle)

# Check the updated data
head(all_data)

# === Split by CWD status ===
unaffected_data <- all_data %>% filter(id %in% unaffected_ids)
affected_data   <- all_data %>% filter(!(id %in% unaffected_ids))

# === Save datasets ===
output_dir <- "<LOCAL_PATH>"

write.csv(unaffected_data, file.path(output_dir, "unaffected_combined.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(affected_data,   file.path(output_dir, "affected_combined.csv"),   row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
split_cwd_ids_manual <- function(train_ids) {
  test_ids <- setdiff(unaffected_ids, train_ids)

  training_data <- all_data %>% filter(id %in% train_ids)
  testing_data  <- all_data %>% filter(
    (id %in% test_ids) |
    (id %notin% unaffected_ids)  # CWD-positive
  )

  list(training_data = training_data, testing_data = testing_data)
}

}
```

```{r}
female_neg  <- setdiff(CWD_Free_clean, male_ids)

# --- Fixed male split ---
train_ids_male <- c(41, 46, 81, 141)
test_ids_male  <- c(55, 58, 120, 92)

# --- Adaptive split function ---
create_balanced_split_adaptive <- function(male_train, male_test, female_inf_ids, female_neg_ids, 
                                            target_inf_rate, train_size = 32, test_size = 32) {
  # Split by infection status
  male_train_inf <- male_train[male_train %in% CWD_Infected_clean]
  male_train_neg <- male_train[male_train %in% CWD_Free_clean]
  male_test_inf  <- male_test[male_test %in% CWD_Infected_clean]
  male_test_neg  <- male_test[male_test %in% CWD_Free_clean]
  
  # Current counts from males
  n_male_train_inf <- length(male_train_inf)
  n_male_train_neg <- length(male_train_neg)
  
  n_male_test_inf  <- length(male_test_inf)
  n_male_test_neg  <- length(male_test_neg)
  
  # Remaining needed from females
  n_needed_train_inf <- max(0, round(train_size * target_inf_rate) - n_male_train_inf)
  n_needed_train_neg <- max(0, train_size - round(train_size * target_inf_rate) - n_male_train_neg)
  
  n_needed_test_inf  <- max(0, round(test_size * target_inf_rate) - n_male_test_inf)
  n_needed_test_neg  <- max(0, test_size - round(test_size * target_inf_rate) - n_male_test_neg)
  
  # Check feasibility and adjust to available pool
  n_needed_train_inf <- min(n_needed_train_inf, length(female_inf_ids))
  n_needed_train_neg <- min(n_needed_train_neg, length(female_neg_ids))
  
  n_needed_test_inf  <- min(n_needed_test_inf, length(female_inf_ids) - n_needed_train_inf)
  n_needed_test_neg  <- min(n_needed_test_neg, length(female_neg_ids) - n_needed_train_neg)
  
  set.seed(123)
  
  train_female_inf <- sample(female_inf_ids, n_needed_train_inf)
  train_female_neg <- sample(female_neg_ids, n_needed_train_neg)
  
  test_female_inf <- sample(setdiff(female_inf_ids, train_female_inf), n_needed_test_inf)
  test_female_neg <- sample(setdiff(female_neg_ids, train_female_neg), n_needed_test_neg)
  
  train_ids <- c(male_train_inf, male_train_neg, train_female_inf, train_female_neg)
  test_ids  <- c(male_test_inf, male_test_neg, test_female_inf, test_female_neg)
  
  # Warnings if actual achieved infection rate deviates more than 5%
  actual_train_rate <- mean(train_ids %in% CWD_Infected_clean)
  actual_test_rate  <- mean(test_ids %in% CWD_Infected_clean)
  
  if (abs(actual_train_rate - target_inf_rate) > 0.05) {
    warning(sprintf("⚠️ Train achieved infection rate %.1f%% deviates from target %.1f%%", actual_train_rate * 100, target_inf_rate * 100))
  }
  if (abs(actual_test_rate - target_inf_rate) > 0.05) {
    warning(sprintf("⚠️ Test achieved infection rate %.1f%% deviates from target %.1f%%", actual_test_rate * 100, target_inf_rate * 100))
  }
  
  return(list(train_ids = train_ids, test_ids = test_ids))
}

# --- Generate splits with adaptive logic only ---
infection_rates <- c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40)
splits <- lapply(infection_rates, function(rate) {
  create_balanced_split_adaptive(train_ids_male, test_ids_male, female_inf, female_neg, rate, train_size = 32, test_size = 32)
})
names(splits) <- paste0("split_", infection_rates * 100)

# --- Sanity checker ---
check_split_sanity <- function(train_ids, test_ids, label) {
  train_inf_rate <- mean(train_ids %in% CWD_Infected_clean)
  test_inf_rate  <- mean(test_ids %in% CWD_Infected_clean)
  cat(sprintf("\n📄 %s — SANITY CHECK", label))
  cat(sprintf("\nTraining: %d IDs (Infected: %.1f%%)", length(train_ids), train_inf_rate * 100))
  cat(sprintf("\nTesting:  %d IDs (Infected: %.1f%%)\n", length(test_ids), test_inf_rate * 100))
}

for (name in names(splits)) {
  check_split_sanity(splits[[name]]$train_ids, splits[[name]]$test_ids, name)
}

# --- Split and save ---
split_manual <- function(train_ids, test_ids) {
  list(
    training_data = all_data %>% filter(id %in% train_ids),
    testing_data  = all_data %>% filter(id %in% test_ids)
  )
}
```
